blurb: Large, heavy-boned Japanese spitz with a bear-like head and curled tail
description: The Akita is a large working breed from the mountains of northern Japan with a thick double coat and curled tail, known as loyal and reserved.
answer: The Akita is a large Japanese working dog of spitz type from the mountains of northern Japan, with a separate American type developed after World War II. It is heavy-boned, with a thick double coat, erect ears and a tail curled over the back, and is generally described as territorial and reserved with strangers.

body: The breed's ancestors were hunting dogs of the Tōhoku region and the Ōdate dog, which was kept as a guard and fighting dog and renamed the Akita Inu in 1931, when it was declared a Japanese natural monument. Crossbreeding nearly wiped out the original type, and breeders rebuilt it after the war. The story of the loyal dog Hachikō and Helen Keller's Akitas brought the breed international fame. Most kennel clubs, including the FCI and, since 2020, the AKC, now treat the Japanese Akita and American Akita as separate breeds.

The Akita is substantial for its height, with heavy bone, small deep-set eyes, triangular erect ears and cat-like feet. American-type males typically stand 66–71 cm and weigh 45–59 kg; the Japanese type is a little smaller and lighter. American Akitas may be any color, while Japanese Akitas are limited to red, fawn, sesame, brindle and white with urajiro markings. A long-coated variety occurs but is a show fault.

The Akita is commonly described as large, strong, independent and dominant, territorial about its property and reserved with strangers. One survey in Poland reported aggression towards other dogs in a majority of the Akitas studied. Some countries' breed-specific legislation lists the Akita as a dangerous dog.
Sources give little detail on daily care or exercise. Today the breed is kept mainly as a companion and also takes part in obedience, tracking, agility and weight-pulling events.

Akitas are generally described as hardy. Conditions reported in the breed include autoimmune diseases such as uveodermatologic syndrome and sebaceous adenitis, hypothyroidism, bloat, progressive retinal atrophy, glaucoma, hip and elbow dysplasia and von Willebrand disease. A UK study found a life expectancy of 11.4 years.

faq.q: How big does an Akita get?
faq.a: Akitas typically stand about 58–70 cm at the shoulder; large American-type males can weigh 45–59 kg.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Akita and the American Akita?
faq.a: American Akitas are generally larger and heavier-boned with a bear-like head and may be any color, while Japanese Akitas are lighter, more fox-like and limited to a few colors.
A commonly cited range is 10–12 years, and one UK study found a life expectancy of 11.4 years.
